claims.text: Equiatomic CoNiCrFeMnNi HEA nanowires exhibit robust temperature-dependent plastic deformation.
Intrinsic lattice distortion contributes to the temperature-dependent deformation behavior of the HEA nanowires.
Multiple slip systems promote a controlled transition between deformation mechanisms as temperature changes.
The as-prepared HEA nanowires are single-phase FCC.
The as-prepared HEA nanowires have a uniform elemental distribution and minimal defects.
Stress-strain behavior of Ag and CoNiCrFeMn HEA nanowires can be evaluated at 77, 300, and 1000 K.
The proposed tests use a constant strain rate across all temperatures.
Differences among constituent atomic lattice parameters create friction that impedes partial-dislocation motion in CoNiCrFeMn HEA nanowires.
The random multielement distribution produces significant variations in atomic interactions.
Lattice distortion and varying atomic interactions mediate FCC-to-HCP transformation and deformation twinning in the HEA nanowires.
At low temperatures, plastic deformation of the HEA nanowires is dominated by partial-dislocation nucleation from free surfaces and twinning.
At high temperatures, thermal activation retards twin propagation in the HEA nanowires.
At high temperatures, thermal activation enables transformation-induced plasticity in the HEA nanowires.
CoNiCrFeMn HEA nanowires exhibit an exceptional strength-ductility trade-off at cryogenic temperatures and retain good flow stress and ductility at high temperatures.
The HEA nanowires retain higher yield strength and ductility than Ag nanowires at both low and high temperatures.
The HEA nanowires exhibit controlled softening and a transition in the governing deformation mechanism as temperature increases.
Ag nanowires exhibit cryogenic-temperature superplasticity associated with reorientation from a (110) to a (100) cross-section.
Ag nanowires have less resistance to high-temperature softening than the HEA nanowires.
Nanoscale size effects promote deformation mechanisms distinct from those in bulk specimens.
The proposed nanoscale behavior should not be extrapolated directly to bulk samples.
